ratings.note: f: 6/6 usability participants struggled to find Change dates (screenshot shows only an unlabelled '...' button); i: detour, restart or phone on a core task; p: once found it is remembered. s=4; rated 3 because restarting from the first page is a cheap workaround that loses only the date fields, so most users recover.

f: only when length exceeds the berth limit (11/100 reporters, 1/6 observed); i: screenshot shows a dead end with code only, no back link, typed data lost, users phone or restart; p: no reason is given so users cannot learn to avoid it ('Error BK-409 again'). s=4.

f: anyone planning by the table in BST months (8/100, 1/6 observed reading UTC as local); i: arrival an hour off the gate, waiting outside or closed gate, though the caption does state UTC; p: learned after the first mistake. s=3.

f: arrival time is chosen in every booking, 2/6 observed picking a closed-gate time; i: booked arrival cannot be made, discovered at the entrance; p: experienced visitors learn to check the gate. s=3.
f: boats with a bowsprit or overhangs only (6/100); i: boat booked into a berth it does not fit, office must correct it and tickets result; p: once told to use LOA it is learned. s=3.
f: skippers who think in feet (4/100, 1/6); i: feet value leads into the BK-409 dead end or a wrong berth the office had to catch (FB-0016, FB-0091); p: learned once. s=3.
f: 3/6 usability participants did not know the term; i: stall or ask, the blocking consequence belongs to the mandatory rule (separate finding); p: once explained it is known. s=2.

f: boats without DSC radio, a minority (5/94); i: screenshot shows Continue blocked by 'Enter the MMSI' with no alternative, so they cannot book online and phone; p: recurs every booking and cannot be overcome. s=4.

f: only users who go Back to the boat page (7/100, 1/6); i: typed data lost, retyped on a phone at sea; p: happens every time. s=4; rated 3 because only four short fields are lost and the task still completes.
f: every booker sees the page, new visitors need the info (7/100, 2/6); i: phone the office or wait outside 40 min (FB-0018); p: returning skippers know the channel and gate. s=3.
f: every user comparing berths sees per-metre rates only (screenshot); i: mental arithmetic, total appears at review; p: recurs each booking but manageable. s=2.
f: headings differ on every journey ('Book a visitor berth' vs 'Choose a pontoon space'), 5/100 report doubt; i: extra checking, no failed bookings reported; p: resolved after first booking. s=2.
f: absent on every booking page; i: uncertainty about remaining steps on poor signal, a short flow so cost is small; p: returning users know the length. s=2.
